title: Onboard the Payments Team
description:
**SITUATION:**

Monday morning **Priya** and **Marco** join the payment box as new engineers. Each needs a login of their own. **payment-handler** sometimes dies overnight, and they need to start it again and see whether it is running. Those are the only admin actions they should have. They must not be able to sign in as root and run other commands.

**The new accounts.** Put both in a new group, `payments-team`, so one rule covers both. Each gets a home directory and the bash shell. Marco reads system logs, so he needs the `adm` group. Do not put either in the `sudo` group. That group can run any command as root.

**What they may run as root.** As root, with no password, they may only restart `payment-handler` and check that it is running. Every other command as root is refused.

**The account that must stop working.** **olek** left last week, but his login still works. Lock the password and set a shell that cannot start a session. Keep `/home/olek` for audit. Do not delete the account.

**YOUR TASK:**

1. Create the group `payments-team`.
2. Create users `priya` and `marco` with home `/home/<name>` and shell `/bin/bash`, both in `payments-team`. Add `marco` to `adm` as well.
3. Let members of `payments-team` run only `systemctl restart payment-handler` and `systemctl status payment-handler` as root, without a password. Put the rule in `/etc/sudoers.d/payments-team`.
4. Lock `olek`'s password and set his shell to `/usr/sbin/nologin`. Keep `/home/olek`.

**SPEC:**

- `/home/priya` and `/home/marco` are owned by those users
- `priya` is not in `adm` or `sudo`; `marco` is not in `sudo`
- `/etc/sudoers.d/payments-team` is `root:root`, mode `440`, and passes `visudo -cf`
- The two allowed commands are the full paths `/usr/bin/systemctl restart payment-handler` and `/usr/bin/systemctl status payment-handler`

**REFERENCES:**

- [DevSetu Blog — Users, Groups, and Permissions](/play/devops-engineer/linux/read/users-groups-and-permissions)

hints: You are learner on a real Ubuntu machine with systemd; sudo works without a password.
Reset gives you a fresh machine (your changes are wiped).
Read SPEC carefully, then Submit — the grader checks the machine itself.
problemStatement.solution:
Priya and Marco need logins on the payment box, and they need to restart **payment-handler** when it dies. That is the only thing they may do as root. Creating accounts and writing a sudo rule both change system files, so these commands use `sudo`.

A group lets one rule cover the whole team. Offboarding locks an account. It does not delete it.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `groupadd` | Creates a group |
| `useradd -m -s -G` | Creates a user, a home directory, a login shell, and extra groups |
| `visudo -f` | Edits a sudoers file and refuses to save it if the syntax is broken |
| `chmod 440` | Root can read the file, and sudo will accept it |
| `usermod -L -s` | Locks the password and changes the login shell |
| `passwd -S` | Shows whether the password is locked (`L`) |

## 1. Group and users

```bash
sudo groupadd payments-team
sudo useradd -m -s /bin/bash -G payments-team priya
sudo useradd -m -s /bin/bash -G payments-team,adm marco
id priya
id marco
```

`-m` creates the home directory. `-G` adds extra groups and leaves the user's own group in place.

## 2. The sudo rule

```bash
sudo visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/payments-team
```

Put this line in the file:

```
%payments-team ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/systemctl restart payment-handler, /usr/bin/systemctl status payment-handler
```

`%` means the rule is for the group. The paths are the full paths of the two commands, so a different `systemctl` on the path cannot slip through.

```bash
sudo chmod 440 /etc/sudoers.d/payments-team
sudo visudo -cf /etc/sudoers.d/payments-team
```

## 3. Offboard olek

```bash
sudo usermod -L -s /usr/sbin/nologin olek
sudo passwd -S olek
```

The second field of `passwd -S` is `L` when the password is locked. Leave `/home/olek` where it is.

Then **Submit**.
